name: Fireflies
description: A dusk meadow full of 600 tiny yellow-green fireflies that are dark between flashes, and the beat grid pulls them into unison as strongly as the beat is clear. Each firefly runs its own clock and flashes when it runs out; a flash nudges every neighbour within about a ninth of the frame height a little closer to its own flash, 60 ms late, so flashes relay across the meadow in visible sweeps (Nicky Case's Fireflies model, CC0). On every beat-grid tick (every 1, 2 or 4 beats, whichever puts the flash cycle nearest one second) each clock is pulled toward the tick and retunes its own period (Ermentrout 1991), scaled by the track's beat clarity: a steady beat locks the swarm onto it within about 15 s, while an irregular beat, or one whose clarity is unknown, leaves the swarm free, where only the neighbour relay runs. Every track starts incoherent by design; the arc is the swarm finding the beat. At near-silence all but 5 % of the fireflies fade out over about 1.5 s; the meadow stays lit. Each flash is a small bright core with a faint halo, 40 ms rise and 0.11 s decay, so a unison flash is hundreds of tiny points rather than a frame-wide lift. FF.1: the behaviour is ported from the FF.0 spike and the world is the spike's placeholder; FF.2 builds the world and FF.3 the light. Not certified, and excluded from manual cycling until then.
author: Matt

audio_routes.note: FF.1 — each beatPhase01 wrap is a grid tick; every m-th tick pulls every clock toward 0 by K·0.30 of its wrapped error and retunes its period by K·0.05. K = clamp(2·stems.beatClarity01 − 1, 0, 1), so unknown (0.5) is free (D-257). beatClarity01 and nearSilent01 (the straggler fade) are not declared here: neither is in AudioRoutePrimitives' recordable map, and the committed route_coverage fixtures predate beatClarity01 and never reach near-silence. Both are gated in FirefliesSwarmTests instead.
